newsitem.title: FRANCE: Crop fears to support world wheat prices - AGPM.
newsitem.headline: Crop fears to support world wheat prices - AGPM.

text.p: Fears of a lower world wheat crop for 1997, if confirmed, are likely to step up pressure on world wheat prices, the French maize growers association AGPM said in its May report.
"The 1997 harvest may be below that for 1996, which would only increase the current tension on world prices," it said.
In early April the International Grains Council targeted a 1997 world soft wheat crop of 583 million tonnes, up 3.5 million tonnes over 1996.
But AGPM said this prediction may soon be revised downwards if fears of crop damage in Europe and in the United States are confirmed.
The AGPM said there was concern persistent drought might hurt wheat production in Europe and in regions located around the Mediterranean and that frost in the United States might limit the U.S. crop.
This explained why the European Union, eager to keep domestic supplies and prices under control, had imposed a tax of 15 Ecus per tonne on daily soft wheat exports last Thursday, it said.
